section: 9 (GET /projects/:id/services/:sid/credentials row; POST start/stop/suspend; GET state rows) and 10 (Service ids, branch-stable)

On oss the id is `pg-db` / `cp-web` on every branch, so the daemon resolves the DEFAULT branch: `insta db url --branch feat` returns main's DSN, `insta db connect --branch feat` opens main, `insta compute status|start|stop web --branch feat` acts on main. The plan makes credentials a new contract route and the e2e relies on `--branch feat` DSNs (08 §6 'feat DSN differs'), so this is a wrong answer, not a 501.

Cloud openapi.yaml:7144-7160 credentials ?branch 'defaults to the service's branch' (a per-branch uuid). oss today src/server.ts:327,347 read (req.query).branch and engine.ts:619-620 computeTarget(branchName) falls back to the default branch. Add a test/server.test.ts region WP5 case: list with ?branch=feat, then GET credentials with the returned id and no query returns feat's DSN; same for state. section: 9 (POST/GET/DELETE /projects/:id/compute/domain rows), decision 25; plans/impl/02-router.md §10 Custom domains
problem: The ComputeDomainResult the plan emits uses a vocabulary the CLI renderer does not accept, so `insta compute check-domain` will always print 'serving not yet' with blockers on oss: (a) `ssl: 'issued'` is not a value the CLI knows; only `ssl === 'active'` reads as issued, anything else is 'pending' plus a blocker; (b) sending `ssl` at all makes the CLI treat the answer as plane-shaped (`reportsOrigin`), so a missing `origin` yields 'UNCONFIRMED' (ready:false) and a missing TXT record yields 'no ownership TXT from the platform'; (c) dns[].status `'pending'` is outside the cloud's DnsRecordCheck set (ok|missing|mismatch|unchecked) and renders as 'unchecked' plus a blocker; (d) local mode `ssl: 'external'` still trips (b).
evidence: insta-cli origin/main src/commands/compute.ts:98-113 (reportsOrigin = r.ssl !== undefined; origin undefined => UNCONFIRMED, ready:false), :158-166 (no TXT && reportsOrigin => blocker), :180-181 (verdictOf: ok | mismatch | missing | else unchecked+blocker), :207-211 (ssl 'active' ok; 'external' no blocker; any other string => pending + blocker), :226-228 (serving only when configured && no blockers). Cloud vocabulary: insta-platform src/adapters/types.ts:271 `DnsRecordCheck = 'ok' | 'missing' | 'mismatch' | 'unchecked'`; src/adapters/insta-compute.ts:1842-1848 (configured = state === 'active', sslStatus passthrough); src/provisioning/deploy.ts:45-49 ComputeDomainResult (ssl?, origin?, edgeOrigin?, originOk?, originStatus? all optional). Plan text: 00 §9 'dns:[{type:'CNAME', name, value:'api.<domain>', note?, status}], service, region:'local', ssl'; 02 §10 'ssl = certFor(h) found -> issued else pending (local mode: external)', 'status ... (ok | pending | unchecked)'.
fix: Emit the Fly-shaped envelope the CLI renders cleanly: OMIT `ssl`, `origin`, `edgeOrigin`, `originOk`, `originStatus` entirely (both modes); put the verdict in `configured` (true when the routing record resolves to us AND, in server mode, the certificate exists in the store; local mode: true when the record resolves); dns[].status in {ok, missing, mismatch, unchecked} (use 'missing' where the plan says 'pending'); `status` in {'pending','ready','not added'} as today. Rewrite 00 §9 row, decision 25 ('ssl: external' -> 'no ssl field; configured reflects the alias') and 02 §10 accordingly, and add to test/server.test.ts region WP2: the domain result has no `ssl` key and dns[].status is one of the four values.

section: 3 Guard, step 4 (CSRF belt); conflicts with plans/impl/08-docs-e2e.md §1.3 (headless setup) and §7 step 3 (server-smoke)
problem: WP1 rejects every cookie-authenticated non-GET request that carries neither an Origin header nor Sec-Fetch-Site with 403. WP8's documented headless setup and the server e2e do exactly that: curl with the sign-up cookie jar, then `POST /tokens {name}` with no Origin. That request 403s, so the e2e step 3 fails and the docs recipe is wrong. The cloud's raw mount (Better Auth) only enforces an allow-list on a PRESENT Origin; a bare curl passes.
evidence: 01 §3.4: 'actor.source === cookie and method not in GET|HEAD|OPTIONS -> require Origin (or Sec-Fetch-Site in same-origin|none) ... else 403'. 08 §1.3: 'headless setup (three curls: POST /api/auth/sign-up/email with a cookie jar, POST /tokens {name}, insta login --api-key)'; 08 §7.3: 'POST /tokens {"name":"ci"} with the jar -> 201'. insta-platform src/auth/betterauth.ts trustedOrigins comment: 'CSRF/redirect allow-list for the mounted handler' (allow-list on the presented Origin, not a presence requirement).
fix: In 01 §3.4 change the rule to: when Origin (or Referer) is PRESENT and its host differs from req.headers.host, 403; when both are absent and Sec-Fetch-Site is absent, allow (non-browser client). Add a server-auth test 'cookie POST without Origin passes; cookie POST with a foreign Origin 403s'. Alternatively keep the strict rule and change 08 §1.3 and §7.3 to pass `-H "Origin: https://console.<domain>"` on every cookie POST, and say so in setup.mdx. Pick one and make both plans agree.

section: §1.4 domains.mdx, §1.7 upgrade.mdx, §3 COMPATIBILITY rows, §7 step 8 (server-smoke); also plans/impl/02-router.md 'Docs facts for WP8' and plans/impl/09-integration-order.md 'What the integrator hands back'

section: §1 Hostnames (assertHostLabel) and §Tests 'a branch name producing a >63-char label -> 400'; plans/impl/00-contract.md §10
problem: A service name the cloud accepts (up to 39 chars, the CLI's own grammar) combined with a frozen ref (two 20-char slugs plus a dash, up to 41 chars) yields labels up to 3+39+1+41 = 84 chars, so `insta services add postgres <long-name>` and `insta branch create <long-name>` that succeed on the cloud answer 400 on oss. The plan turns a DNS constraint into a contract divergence instead of bounding the label.
evidence: insta-cli origin/main src/commands/services.ts:7 `SERVICE_NAME_RE = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,38}$/`; oss src/engine.ts:12 `slug(...).slice(0, 20)`, :47 ref = `${projectSlug}-${slug(branch)}`; plan 02 §1 'assertHostLabel: ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ ... 400'; 00 §10 'Every label matches ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$'.
fix: Have `hostFor` produce a bounded label instead of rejecting: keep the readable prefix and, when the label would exceed 63 chars, truncate and append a short stable hash (e.g. 6 hex of sha256 over the full label) so `<group>-<ref>` stays unique and deterministic; record the minted host on the row (`apps[g].host`, `databases[id].host`) so nothing re-derives it. Keep the 400 only for the operator-supplied custom-domain hostname. Update the 02 test line and 08 domains.mdx to describe the bound.

section: 9 (POST /projects/:id/services row) and plans/impl/05-templates-parity.md §3 Registrations
problem: The per-type cap error text is specified as `branch has reached the limit of 5 <type> services`; the cloud's text is `branch has reached this plan's limit of N <type> services` followed by an upgrade hint. The CLI prints the message verbatim, so scripts or docs that match on it diverge for no reason.

Plan 00 §9: '400 'branch has reached the limit of 5 <type> services''; 05 §3: 'cap ... -> 400 branch has reached the limit of <cap> postgres services'.

section: Algorithm > wake(key, { door }) and > Op bookkeeping
problem: A traffic wake is not fenced against an in-flight deploy, lifecycle op or sleep on the same key. `wake()` only checks the `wakes` singleflight map, then reads live container state and calls `runtime.start`. Router wakes (`engine.wake(key,{door:'traffic'})`) bypass `serialize()` (only `deploy`/`lifecycle`/`restart` go through the per-app chain), so `docker start` can race `deployLocked`'s `docker rm -f` + `docker create` on the same container name, and a wake that lands during a `sleep()` (docker stop in flight) sees `running`, probes true, returns, and the held request is proxied to a container that is stopping. `opsInFlight` is a counter, not awaitable, so there is nothing to wait on. `wake()` also has no branch for a container that is absent from `containers()` (removed by a concurrent deploy).
evidence: 03-scheduler.md:29 `opsInFlight: Map<key, number>`; :51 `sleep()`: 'wake or op in flight -> false' (one direction only); :60-61 `wake()` step 2 checks `wakes` only, step 3 `opsInFlight++; state = live containers().get(container)` with cases running|paused|exited|created|dead|restarting and no undefined case; :78 'serialize() stays the mutual exclusion; withOp is the sweep-visible flag' (traffic wakes never enter serialize). src/engine.ts:33-37 `serialize` is per `${b.id}:${group}`; 02-router.md:46 the HTTP lane calls `deps.wake(route)` directly.
fix: In `Scheduler`: make `withOp` store `Map<key, Promise<void>>` (settled when the op ends) alongside the counter; `wake()` step 2a awaits `sleeps.get(key)` and every in-flight op promise for the key before reading state, then re-reads `stateCache`/`targets()` (a deploy that just ran ends in `onUp`, so the wake becomes a no-op). Add an explicit case: container absent from `containers()` -> throw `Error('service has no container (deploy in progress or removed)')` mapped to 503 by the router, never `runtime.start`. Make `stateOf(key)` return `'asleep'` while a sleep promise is pending so the router deterministically takes the wake path instead of dialling a stopping container. Add `test/scheduler.test.ts` cases: 'wake during sleep waits for the stop then starts', 'wake during withOp waits for the op and does not call runtime.start when the op ended in onUp'.

section: Algorithm > 11. Engine seams (allocLanes / assertHostFree) and 00-contract.md 7.1 WP2
problem: Lane-port allocation and hostname reservation are check-then-act across awaits with no serialization. `allocLanes` picks 'the lowest free port across all branch.lanes' at the start of `provisionBranch`, but the branch row (with `lanes`) is only written by `mutate` at the end, after `db.provision`/`db.fork` (seconds). Two concurrent `branch create` or `services add postgres` calls on different projects both get port 20000. `buildTable` then throws on the duplicate (`byPort`/duplicate host -> throw), which kills routing for every service on the next `table()` rebuild. `createProject` and `createBranch` have no `serialize` key (only deploy/lifecycle/restart do), so nothing prevents the overlap. Same shape for `assertHostFree` at `addComputeService`/`addDbService` and for `createProject`'s slug check.
evidence: 02-router.md:81 'allocLanes ... lowest free port in cfg.lanes.portRange across all branch.lanes'; 02-router.md:39 'Duplicate host -> throw (engine guards prevent it ...)'; 05-templates-parity.md §4 provisionBranch: `lanes = this.allocLanes(...)` first, row written last; src/engine.ts:66-104 (`provisionBranch` awaits db/storage/managed before `mutate`), :33-37 (`serialize` only keyed per app), :128-135 (`createBranch` not serialized).
fix: Reserve inside one `mutate`: `allocLanes` writes the chosen ports into `state.branches[<pending id>].lanes` (or a `state.laneReservations: Record<port, branchId>` region WP2) synchronously before any await, and the compensation path releases them; generate the branch id before provisioning so the reservation has an owner. Likewise `assertHostFree` + registration push happen in the same `mutate` before the container work. Add an engine-wide `serialize('provision')` chain around `provisionBranch`, `addDbService`, `addStorageService`, `addManagedService`, `addComputeService`, `createProject` so name/port reservations are linear. `buildTable` must never throw at request time: on a duplicate, log and keep the first route. Add a `test/server.test.ts` region WP2 test: two concurrent `POST /branches` on two projects yield distinct lane ports; a fake table build with a duplicate does not throw.

section: Algorithm > src/upstream.ts and 00-contract.md 8.1
problem: The upstream address cache is keyed per container name with no TTL and is only invalidated by the scheduler's own sleep/wake (`onUp`/`onAsleep` -> forget) or a dial error. On a user-defined bridge network a container that restarts on its own (`--restart unless-stopped` after a crash, `docker restart` by an operator) can get a different IP; the freed IP can be reassigned to another container on the same network (another branch's postgres joins nothing, but a compute container of the same branch, or Garage which is connected to every branch network, can take it). A stale entry then splices a client to the wrong backend. Because a fork inherits the source's password (decision 18), a mis-routed `pg-db-shop-feat` connection to `shop-main`'s postgres authenticates and reads/writes the wrong branch. The 'refuses -> forget and re-resolve once' rule only catches ECONNREFUSED, not a successful connect to the wrong container.
evidence: 00-contract.md:562 'Cached per container'; :564 forget 'called by the scheduler after every sleep/wake and by the router on dial errors'; 03-scheduler.md:91 resolve via `docker inspect ... IPAddress`; 02-router.md:47 'on a cache hit that refuses, re-resolve once'; 00-contract.md:79 decision 18 'a fork inherits the source's files and therefore its password'.
fix: Give cache entries a short TTL (e.g. `cfg.lanes.touchDebounceMs`, 5 s) and store the container `.Id` + `.State.StartedAt` from the same `docker inspect`; the sweep, which already runs `docker ps -a` every 30 s, adds `{{.ID}}` to its format and calls `upstream.forget` for any container whose id changed. In server mode also pass `--ip` from a per-branch-network deterministic address? (heavier; optional). Add `test/upstream.test.ts` cases: 'entry expires after TTL', 'sweep forgets a container whose id changed'. Document in 03 that resolve is ~10 ms so the TTL costs nothing measurable.

section: Algorithm > Stamp writers (register) and > Boot reconcile
problem: Create grace is measured from the in-memory ledger's `createdAt`, which `register()` sets to `now` 'when absent', and boot reconcile registers every target. So every daemon restart (every upgrade, every compose recreate) gives every running service a fresh 10-minute create grace on top of the idle window: after a restart nothing sleeps for at least 10 min + 5 min. The cloud's grace is on the row's creation time; only the ready stamp resets. `ServiceTarget.createdAt` already exists in the contract and is unused for this.
evidence: 03-scheduler.md:33-35 'register(key): createdAt = lastActiveAt = now when absent'; :37-38 boot reconcile 'Every target gets register(key) (full window after a restart)'; :44 sweep condition `now - createdAt >= createGraceSec*1000`; 00-contract.md:608 `ServiceTarget { ... createdAt: number }`; :71 decision 10 'a restart stamps every service at boot'.
fix: Drop `createdAt` from the ledger record; the sweep reads `target.createdAt` (compute: `serviceSettings[sid].createdAt ?? apps[g].updatedAt`, postgres: `dbServices[].createdAt`, managed: `managedServices[].createdAt`, else branch `createdAt`). `register(key)` sets only `lastActiveAt = now`. Add to `test/scheduler.test.ts`: 'a service created 20 min ago sleeps one idle window after a boot reconcile, not create grace + window'.

section: Algorithm > evictForRoom and > Boot reconcile
problem: Eviction can thrash and can evict actively serving services. (a) Wake protection is soft ('prefer those with now - wokeAt >= wakeProtectSec'): when only recently woken services are running, the pass still evicts one, so two services that do not fit together ping-pong on every request. (b) The pressure pass has no idleness floor: the victim is the oldest `lastActiveAt` among ALL running non-alwaysOn services, so under sustained load on a box below the 15 percent floor a service with a request in flight (ticker stamping every 5 s) is stopped, its traffic wakes it 1 s later, and the next victim goes. (c) 'one pressure pass runs immediately' at boot, before any `docker stats` sample and with every `lastActiveAt` equal to boot time, so a restart on a busy box stops arbitrary running services. (d) `wake()` awaits the victim's `docker stop -t 30` before `docker start`, adding up to 30 s to the hold.
evidence: 03-scheduler.md:55 'prefer those with now - wokeAt >= wakeProtectSec*1000; empty -> log once per sweep and return; victim = oldest lastActiveAt'; :40 'one pressure pass runs immediately'; :61 wake step 3 `evictForRoom(need, {key})` then `runtime.start`; designs/wp3.json evictForRoom step b 'protected alone if the rest is empty'.
fix: Make protection hard: never evict a service with `now - wokeAt < wakeProtectSec*1000` or `now - lastActiveAt < 2*touchDebounceMs` (has traffic right now) or an in-flight HTTP request/TCP splice (router exposes `inFlight(key)` via touch bookkeeping); when the pool is empty, log and let the wake proceed (the kernel is the last resort, as the plan already accepts). Skip the boot pressure pass (first pass runs on the first sweep tick after `docker stats` has a sample). In `wake()`, fire `evictForRoom` and `runtime.start` concurrently (stop grace for eviction victims may use `stopGraceSec` not `stopGraceDbSec`). Add tests: 'two services that do not fit do not ping-pong within wakeProtectSec', 'a service stamped 3 s ago is never a victim', 'boot performs no eviction'.

section: 7.2 Edit points (liveState row) vs 03-scheduler.md > View mapping and > Tests (region WP3)
problem: Two sources of truth for compute runtime state. Contract 7.2 keeps `liveState()` on the adapter (`compute.state` = docker inspect, 'adapter stopped + sleptAt set + desired running -> suspended'), while 03 says the view mapping is 'implemented once in rowRuntime/liveState/healthOverlay' from `stateOf` and `services()` drops the docker read. The fake compute adapter returns `state: async () => 'running'` unconditionally, and the existing lifecycle test asserts `state: 'running'` after a stop for that reason. The WP3 test 'after scheduler.sleep: GET state {desiredState:running, state:suspended}' cannot pass with the adapter-based `liveState` and the fixed fake, and if `liveState` moves to `stateOf`, the existing test at server.test.ts:475-489 (`state: 'running'` after stop) breaks, contradicting 'existing lifecycle tests (lines 475-662) unchanged and green'.
evidence: 00-contract.md:547 liveState row; :437 fakes `state: async () => 'running'`; 03-scheduler.md:75 'Implemented once in rowRuntime(key) / liveState / healthOverlay'; :119 test 'after scheduler.sleep: GET state {desiredState:'running', state:'suspended'}'; :124 'existing lifecycle tests (lines 475-662) unchanged and green'; test/server.test.ts:475-489 expects `state: 'running'` after stop; src/engine.ts:709-710 `liveState` = `compute.state`.
fix: Pick one: `liveState(key)` reads `scheduler.stateOf(key)` (Runtime.containers is the single docker read) and `ComputeAdapter.state` is deleted from the interface (contract §4). In `test/fakes.ts` the `FakeRuntime` is the single fake state store and `makeEngine` wires it; update 03's test list to say the existing lifecycle assertions at 475-489 change from `state: 'running'` to `state: 'stopped'` after stop (list it as an allowed existing-assertion edit in 03 and 09), and list `compute.state` removal in the scaffold step so `restart-policy.test.ts` is not affected.

section: Algorithm > D. Postgres fork, > F. Legacy migration, > G. Teardown
problem: Crash recovery leaves unrecoverable orphans. (a) A daemon crash during `createBranch` (after `docker run` of the clone container or during `clonePostgres`) leaves `io-<ref>-pg-<name>` and a partial `pg/<ref>/<dataId>` with no state row; the boot only logs orphan dirs (delete needs `INSTA_OSS_SWEEP_ORPHANS=1`, never set), and the fork path has no dst emptiness check and no pre-existing-container removal, so the user's retry of `branch create feat` fails on 'name already in use' or clones over a half-copied directory forever. (b) Legacy migration step 1 skips the whole postgres step when the legacy container is 'absent'; a crash after `docker rm -f -v <c>` but before the re-create leaves the data in the target dir, no container, `databases[id].container` still the legacy name, `dataVersion` undefined: every boot skips it again and every DB call fails.
evidence: 04-branching.md:33 provision `assertEmptyOrMissing(t.dataDir)` but D step 2 (line ~43) runs `data.clonePostgres(src.dataDir, dst.dataDir)` then `docker run` with no dst check and no `rm -f` of a stale container; :64 'Boot logs orphan dirs ...; deletes only with INSTA_OSS_SWEEP_ORPHANS=1'; :57 'legacy container io-<ref>-pg (or databases[id].container); absent -> skip' then 'docker rm -f -v <c>; re-create'; :60 'Idempotent and resumable'.
fix: D step 2: before the copy, `docker rm -f` any container named `dst.container` that no branch row references, and if `dst.dataDir` is non-empty and unreferenced, `data.remove(dst)` first (log 'removing orphan from an interrupted fork'); same guard in `provision`. F step 1: the skip condition becomes 'legacy container absent AND new container present'; when the legacy container is absent but `hasPgData(target)` and the new container is missing, run the re-create step. Add `test/datadir-migrate.test.ts` case 'legacy gone, target has PG_VERSION, new container missing -> re-create plan' and `test/postgres-adapter.test.ts` case 'fork onto a non-empty unreferenced dst removes it first'.

section: Algorithm > 0. Listeners per mode (table() / invalidate())
problem: Lane listeners are created only when the route table is rebuilt, and the table is rebuilt lazily inside `table()` on the next request. After `services add postgres analytics` in local mode (a new lane port) or a new MySQL service in server mode, nothing listens on the new port until some other request happens to hit the router; `insta db url` followed by `psql` gets ECONNREFUSED. `router.invalidate()` only drops the cache. `addDbService` in 05 does not even call `invalidate()` (only rename does).
evidence: 02-router.md:30 'table(): if (cached && cached.rev === loadState().rev) return cached.table; rebuild. invalidate() drops the cache. Lane listeners are reconciled against the table on every rebuild'; 05-templates-parity.md §3 addDbService lists `scheduler.register` and `emit` but no `router.invalidate`.
fix: `invalidate()` rebuilds the table and reconciles listeners synchronously (or schedules `setImmediate(reconcile)`), and the engine calls `this.router.invalidate()` after every `mutate` that changes hosts or lanes (`provisionBranch`, `addDbService`, `addStorageService`, `addManagedService`, `addComputeService`, renames, removes, domain CRUD, `destroyBranch`). Add to `test/router.test.ts`: 'a route added to state and invalidate() results in a listening port before any request'.

section: Algorithm > 7. state.json discipline and 02-router.md > 0 (table()) / 8.2 RouterDeps.intent
problem: Every proxied request and every TCP connection does a full `structuredClone` of state.json: `table()` calls `loadState().rev` to check its cache and `intent(route)` reads `desiredState` from `loadState()`, and the plan makes every `loadState()` cache hit return a clone. `events` is unbounded and the scheduler now emits `service.sleep`/`service.wake` automatically (plus `touchLater` every 30 s bumps `rev`, forcing a table rebuild even when routing did not change). The router and API share one event loop, so a state file with thousands of events costs milliseconds of blocking per request and grows without bound; `saveState` rewrites the whole file synchronously on every event.
evidence: 01-identity-config.md:94 'cache hit -> structuredClone'; 02-router.md:30 `cached.rev === loadState().rev`; 00-contract.md:590 `intent(route)` 'engine desiredState'; :389 `events: AuditEvent[]` with no cap; :100 decision 39 scheduler event kinds; src/engine.ts:51-56 `emit` = `mutate` (full sync rewrite).
fix: state.ts exports `stateRev(): number` (no clone) and an `onSave(cb)` hook; the router keys its cache on `stateRev()` and stores `desiredState` on the `Route` at build time (rebuild on rev change), so a request path touches no state clone. Cap `events` in `emit` (keep the newest N, e.g. 5000, per state; make N a constant in state.ts) and note it in COMPATIBILITY. Have `touchLater` writes and `emit` bump a separate `auditRev` so routing-irrelevant writes do not rebuild the table. Add `test/state-lock.test.ts`: 'stateRev does not clone; events capped'.

section: 1.1 Scaffold, 1.3 Region markers, 7.2 Edit points; 09-integration-order.md Merge 1 and Merge 2 rebase notes
problem: Parallel implementers will conflict because the shared skeletons are owned by packages that land later than the ones editing them. (a) WP5 (merge 2) lands the `provisionBranch`/`createBranch`/`deployLocked`/`services()` skeleton with the `// filled by WPn` identity hooks, yet WP2/WP3/WP4 branch from the scaffold and must edit those methods directly to test anything, then re-apply at rebase ('re-apply their edits as hook bodies only'). (b) WP1 rewrites `src/main.ts` and `src/state.ts`, moving the scaffold's region markers; every other package's main.ts/state.ts lines then conflict at rebase (09 admits this). (c) `src/adapters/compute.ts`, `postgres.ts`, `manageddb.ts` have three editors each (WP2 args, WP3 limits/grace, WP4 mounts/rewrite) and appear in no region-marker list. (d) `isApiPath` (server.ts:670) is edited by WP1 ('/api', '/auth', '/templates', '/template-deployments', '/tls') and WP5 ('/templates', '/template-deployments'): same line, two owners. (e) The 501 stubs WP3 deletes (server.ts:503-505) and WP2 deletes (509-511) are 3 lines apart, inside one git hunk context; likewise the 501 sweep array in test/server.test.ts:226-228 is edited by WP1, WP2 and WP3. (f) `.github/workflows/ci.yml` gets appended by WP4 and WP6 at the same end-of-file point.
evidence: 05-templates-parity.md:3 'this package lands the structural engine rewrite every later package hooks into'; 09-integration-order.md:23 and :29 rebase notes; 00-contract.md:18 marker file list (no adapters); 01-identity-config.md:59 `isApiPath` list vs 05-templates-parity.md §Files 'isApiPath gains /templates, /template-deployments'; 01-identity-config.md:26 'delete the inline /me (line 55) and /tokens 501s (58-60)'; src/server.ts:503-511; test/server.test.ts:226-228.
fix: Move to the scaffold (step 0): the engine hook skeleton (every `// filled by WPn` identity hook and the rewritten `deployLocked` argument object) so WP2/3/4 fill bodies from day one; the WP1 `main.ts` boot skeleton with all regions in final order and the `state.ts` shape (`initStatePath`, `rev`, stubs) with WP1 filling bodies; `// ---- args WPn ----` marker lines inside `deploy()`/`provision()` in the three adapters (WP4's postgres rewrite must preserve them); an exported `API_PREFIXES` array in server.ts with one marked line per WP; relocate the to-be-replaced 501 stubs (server.ts:58-60, 503-505, 509-511) into regions A/C/B now with no behaviour change; split the 501 sweep array into per-region sub-arrays concatenated; anchor comments `# ---- WP4 ----` / `# ---- WP6 ----` in ci.yml. Update 09 step 0 and remove the two rebase notes.

section: Merge 4 and 'Docker test sequence' (idle knobs) and 00-contract.md §14 / decision 12
problem: Docker suites and the e2e are told to disable the sweep with `INSTA_OSS_IDLE_COMPUTE_SEC=0 INSTA_OSS_IDLE_DB_SEC=0`, but those knobs only disable the idle candidates; the pressure pass (`evictForRoom(0, ...)` on every 30 s tick, plus the immediate boot pass) still runs. On a CI runner or laptop with MemAvailable below 15 percent (common on 7 GiB GitHub runners with Docker images loaded), the scheduler stops the very containers the test is asserting on, producing flaky failures unrelated to the code under test.
evidence: 09-integration-order.md:37 and :72; 03-scheduler.md:132; 00-contract.md:73 decision 12; 03-scheduler.md:47 sweep step 4 `evictForRoom(0, new Set())` unconditional; :40 boot pressure pass.
fix: Every Docker suite and e2e step that does not test sleep sets `INSTA_OSS_SCHEDULER=0` (ticker off; wake/sleep on demand still work) instead of, or in addition to, the idle knobs; `test/sleep-wake.int.test.ts` sets `INSTA_OSS_RAM_FLOOR_PCT=0` (eviction disabled) unless it tests eviction, where it uses `INSTA_OSS_MEM_BUDGET_MB`. Update 09 (Merge 4, Docker test sequence), 00-contract §14, 03 Done-when, and 08 e2e knobs accordingly.

section: Algorithm > 8. instad --reset-admin; 00-contract.md §5 initStatePath and §6 testConfig/makeEngine
problem: (a) `--reset-admin` 'runs without the lock' and mutates state.json from a second process while the daemon may be running; the daemon's next `mutate` (from its stat-keyed cache, or a `touchLater` flush) can overwrite the reset (lost update), or the daemon serves with an admin the operator just deleted until its cache notices. (b) The state path is a module-level singleton set by `initStatePath`, while decision 1 says configs are injected with no singleton; `testConfig()` passes `INSTA_OSS_STATE` into `loadConfig` but nothing in `makeEngine`/`resetFakes` is specified to call `initStatePath(cfg.statePath)`, so a test's engine reads whatever `process.env.INSTA_OSS_STATE` (or `~/.insta-oss/state.json`) says, not the config's path.
evidence: 01-identity-config.md:100 'Runs without the lock'; :95 acquireLock; 00-contract.md:397 `initStatePath` 'main.ts calls before the first loadState; INSTA_OSS_STATE env stays the fallback'; :442-445 `testConfig`/`makeEngine`/`resetFakes` (no initStatePath); :62 decision 1 'No module-level singleton'.
fix: `--reset-admin` acquires the lock like a normal boot and exits with 'stop the daemon first (docker compose stop instad) then re-run' when it is held; document the command as `docker compose run --rm instad --reset-admin` after a stop. `resetFakes()`/`makeEngine()` call `initStatePath(cfg.statePath)` and the contract states one state path per test process (vitest `pool: 'forks'` already isolates files); tests needing two configs in one file must share `statePath`. Add to `test/state-lock.test.ts`: 'reset-admin refuses while the lock is held'.

section: 8.1 Upstream, 8.2 RouterDeps, 8.3 Scheduler constructor; 03-scheduler.md > Stamp writers and > DockerRuntime; 02-router.md > 8 Certificates and Tests
problem: Fake-adapter tests for the router and scheduler need seams the contract does not provide. (a) `RouterDeps.upstream` is typed as the concrete `Upstream` class, whose constructor takes `cfg` and shells out to docker; `test/router.test.ts` ('node servers on ephemeral ports, fake deps') needs a fake that resolves to the test server. (b) The scheduler's `onUp` calls `upstream.forget(container)` and `DockerRuntime.probe` uses `upstream.dial`, but neither `new Scheduler(runtime, cfg, targets, hooks)` nor `new DockerRuntime(cfg)` receives an `Upstream`; the router must share the SAME instance for cache invalidation to work, and nothing says who constructs it. (c) `certFor`/`triggerIssuance` hard-wire `tls.connect` to `127.0.0.1:${edgePort}` and the server-mode pg lane test needs 'a test cert' but no fixture or generator is specified (no openssl in the daemon, Node has no cert API).
evidence: 00-contract.md:594 `upstream: Upstream`; :620 Scheduler constructor without upstream; 03-scheduler.md:33 `onUp(key): ... upstream.forget(container)`; :104-105 DockerRuntime; 02-router.md:69 triggerIssuance; :98 'TLS with a test cert'; 00-contract.md:444 makeEngine wiring lists data and scheduler only.
fix: Declare `export interface UpstreamLike { resolve; forget; dial }` in `src/upstream.ts`; type `RouterDeps.upstream`, `Scheduler` (add a 5th constructor arg `upstream: UpstreamLike`) and `DockerRuntime(cfg, upstream)` on it; `EngineOptions` gains `upstream?: UpstreamLike` and main.ts constructs one `Upstream` handed to `DockerRuntime`, `Scheduler` and `Router`. `test/fakes.ts` (WP3 region) adds `FakeUpstream` (map container -> {host,port}) wired by `makeEngine`. `certs.ts` takes `{ certDir, issue: (host) => Promise<void> }` so tests inject a no-op issuer; check in `test/fixtures/router-test.crt|.key` (self-signed, long-lived, CN router.test) in Caddy's directory layout for the pg/SNI lane tests, generated once by the integrator (documented command in 02).

section: Algorithm > 4. Branch provisioning and cloning (createBranch)
problem: `createBranch` is specified as `withOp(keysOf(source) ∪ keysOf(new))` before `provisionBranch`, but the new branch's id (and therefore its ServiceKeys `${branchId}:${serviceId}`) is minted inside `provisionBranch` (`randomUUID()`), so `keysOf(new)` cannot be computed where the plan places it. Also `evictForRoom` has no create-grace or in-flight-fork check, so the freshly readied clone postgres can be evicted between `db.fork` returning and `sleepNewBranch` (harmless) while the SOURCE postgres is protected only by `withOp`, which is what makes the id ordering matter.
evidence: 05-templates-parity.md:48 `withOp(keysOf(source) ∪ keysOf(new))` then `provisionBranch(...)`; src/engine.ts:98-99 `id: randomUUID()` inside provisionBranch; 03-scheduler.md:55 evictForRoom pool has no createdAt/op check beyond 'nothing in flight'.
fix: Mint `branchId` in `createBranch` (pass it to `provisionBranch(project, name, isDefault, source, branchId)`), so `withOp` can cover both key sets from the start; `provisionBranch` registers the new keys under the already-open op. State it in 05 §4 and in contract 7.2's provisionBranch row.

section: Algorithm > 3. HTTP lane step 4 and Files (wake.ts awaitWake); 00-contract.md 8.2
problem: Two singleflights and two timeouts per wake: the router keeps its own 'wake singleflight map' and `awaitWake(route.key, () => deps.wake(route), wakeTimeoutSec*1000)`, while `Scheduler.wake` is already singleflight per key with the same `wakeTimeoutSec` deadline. The router's timer fires at the same instant as the scheduler's, so which error the client sees is a race; the router map entry is cleared on its timeout while the scheduler promise continues, and the next request creates a second router entry that joins the same scheduler wake, so the hold can exceed 60 s by up to another `probeWindowMs + readyWindowMs` (8 s + 30 s).
evidence: 02-router.md:17 'the wake singleflight map'; :18 `awaitWake`; :46 `await awaitWake(route.key, () => deps.wake(route), wakeTimeoutSec*1000)` then `probePort(up, probeWindowMs)`; :48 readiness retry within `readyWindowMs`; 03-scheduler.md:60 scheduler singleflight; 00-contract.md:167 wakeTimeoutSec 'router hold bound and scheduler readiness bound'.
fix: Delete the router's singleflight and timer; the HTTP/TCP lanes call `deps.wake(route)` directly and map `WakeTimeoutError` -> 504 / `57P03`, `ServiceStoppedError` -> 503. Make the total hold explicit: `wakeTimeoutSec` bounds the scheduler wake, and the post-wake `probeWindowMs`/`readyWindowMs` are documented as additive in 02 Docs facts and 08 sleep.mdx ('held up to 60 s, plus up to 38 s of readiness retries').

section: Algorithm > 1. Boot step 8 (SIGTERM) and > 7 acquireLock; 06-packaging.md compose stop_grace_period
problem: Shutdown ordering can hang past the 30 s compose grace and then crash-loop on the lock. `await app.close()` runs first; Fastify's default close waits for keep-alive connections and in-flight requests, and the router's held wake requests (up to 60 s) and long-lived SSE/WebSocket/pg splices live on that same `node:http`/net servers, so `close()` can exceed `stop_grace_period: 30s`; the container is SIGKILLed, `releaseLock` never runs (touchLater buffer lost), the lock file has a heartbeat under 60 s old, and the replacement container's `acquireLock` throws and exits; compose restarts it until the 60 s stale window passes.
evidence: 01-identity-config.md:42 'SIGTERM/SIGINT: await app.close(), scheduler.stop(), router.stop(), releaseLock()'; :95 'on EEXIST: mtime older than 60 s -> unlink and retry once, else throw'; 06-packaging.md compose `stop_grace_period: 30s`; 02-router.md:65 splice idle 900 s.
fix: Order: `router.stop()` first (stop accepting, destroy lane sockets and held wakes with a 503/ErrorResponse), then `scheduler.stop()`, then `app.close()` with `forceCloseConnections: 'idle'` and a 10 s bound (`Promise.race` with a timer), then `releaseLock()`; `acquireLock` on EEXIST with a fresh heartbeat waits and retries every 2 s up to 60 s before throwing (the container restart case). Add to `test/state-lock.test.ts`: 'a fresh lock is taken over once its heartbeat stops'.

section: Algorithm > 3. HTTP lane step 3 (ticker) and 01-identity-config.md > 2 (sign-in limiter)
problem: Two unbounded per-request allocations. (a) One `setInterval` per in-flight HTTP request/upgraded socket for the 5 s activity ticker: a thousand long-poll or SSE clients means a thousand timers, each firing `touch` for the same key. (b) The sign-in failure limiter `Map<ip, number[]>` is only cleared on success; every IP that fails once (a scan against a public `api.<domain>`) leaves an entry forever.
evidence: 02-router.md:45 'ticker every touchDebounceMs until res (or the upgraded socket) closes'; 01-identity-config.md:53 'Map<ip, number[]> of failure timestamps within 15 min; ... success clears the ip'.
fix: One shared 5 s ticker in the router over a `Map<ServiceKey, count>` of in-flight requests (increment on start, decrement on close; the ticker touches every key with count > 0). In the limiter, prune entries whose newest timestamp is older than 15 min on each insert and cap the map at, say, 10000 IPs (drop oldest). Add a router test 'N concurrent requests on one key create one timer'.

section: A. Boot (probe) and D. Postgres fork (copy engine); contract decision 23 and run-mode matrix row 'Copy engine'
problem: The in-process copy engine cannot produce reflinks on macOS at all, and the boot probe is fatal there. Node's fs.copyFile with COPYFILE_FICLONE_FORCE returns ENOSYS on darwin (libuv refuses FORCE on macOS), and COPYFILE_FICLONE (non-force) silently does a byte copy on APFS. So the plan's probe hits 'any other error is fatal' and the daemon refuses to boot in local mode on macOS; even if ENOSYS were mapped to reflink=false, every fork would stream pg_basebackup and the 'Done when' bullet (APFS 250 MiB fork under 10 s, db.method reflink) can never pass.
evidence: Measured on this machine (darwin, node v22.22.0, APFS): copyFileSync(a,b,COPYFILE_FICLONE_FORCE) -> ENOSYS; copyFileSync with COPYFILE_FICLONE on 512 MiB -> 739 ms vs plain copy 656 ms (no clone); `/bin/cp -c` on the same file -> 24 ms (clonefile). Plan text: plans/impl/04-branching.md:23 ('copyFileSync(src, dst, COPYFILE_FICLONE_FORCE); success -> reflink: true; ENOTSUP|EXDEV|EINVAL|EOPNOTSUPP -> false; any other error is fatal'), :44 (clone step ii uses COPYFILE_FICLONE_FORCE, 'ENOTSUP|EXDEV -> exit 75'), :113 (Done when on APFS); plans/impl/00-contract.md:84 (decision 23 'WP4's Node copy in-process (root in the container, or macOS)'), :712 ('Copy engine: in-process (macOS)').
fix: In 04 §A.1 and §B/§D and contract decision 23: on `process.platform === 'darwin'` the copy engine is Apple's `/bin/cp -c` (clonefile), not fs.copyFile: probe = `execFile('/bin/cp', ['-c', src, dst])` in `.probe/` (non-zero exit -> reflink:false); `fsclone.cjs clone --pg` on darwin copies each file with `cp -c` (same ordering: pg_control first, pg_wal last, scrub list unchanged) and `--reflink=auto` falls back to fs.copyFile on cp failure. Add ENOSYS to the 'no reflink' error set on every platform. Update contract §11 row 'Copy engine' to 'in-process FICLONE (Linux root) | cp -c (macOS) | helper container (unprivileged Linux)'. Add a fsclone.test.ts case 'darwin engine uses /bin/cp -c and reports method reflink only when cp exits 0'.

section: E. install.sh step 5 (fstab entry) together with 04-branching.md C.2 (`-v` bind mounts) and contract §12 last paragraph
problem: A reboot where the XFS loop image fails to mount (fstab has `nofail`) lets dockerd auto-restart every `--restart unless-stopped` postgres/managed container before instad is up; `-v <hostPath>:/var/lib/postgresql/data` makes dockerd CREATE the missing host directory, so the postgres entrypoint runs initdb on an empty directory on the root filesystem and every branch database comes up empty (mysql/mongo likewise). The daemon-side PG_VERSION guard in §B never runs on this path because dockerd, not instad, starts the containers.
evidence: plans/impl/06-packaging.md:138 ('fstab `$IMG $DATA xfs loop,nofail 0 0`'); plans/impl/04-branching.md:34 ('docker run -d --restart unless-stopped ... -v <t.dataDir>:/var/lib/postgresql/data'); plans/impl/00-contract.md:731 ('Docker recreates a missing bind source as an empty directory, so Postgres starts only when PG_VERSION exists' - the guard is in-daemon only). Docker documents that `-v` creates a missing host path as an empty directory while `--mount type=bind` errors instead.
fix: 04 §C.2, §D, §E and manageddb/compute mount lines: use `--mount type=bind,src=<hostPath>,dst=<containerPath>` for every data bind (a missing source then fails the start instead of creating an empty dir). 06 §E.5: write the fstab line as `$IMG $DATA xfs loop,nofail,x-systemd.required-by=docker.service,x-systemd.before=docker.service 0 0` so docker.service does not start when the data mount is absent; add a `test/install.test.ts` assertion on the fstab line and a `test/postgres-adapter.test.ts` assertion that provision emits `--mount type=bind` and never `-v` for the data dir.

section: Decision 20 and §10 table row 'Public bucket' / 'AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3'; 02-router.md §2 (table build) and §3 step 1
problem: With `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3 = https://s3.<domain>` most SDKs (AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 by default, any client without forcePathStyle) send virtual-hosted requests to `https://<bucket>.s3.<domain>/<key>` with a SigV4 Authorization header. The router sends every `*.s3.<domain>` host to Garage's web endpoint (3902), which only serves unsigned GETs of public buckets, so signed PUT/GET/LIST from apps fail or leak to the public web path. Today this cannot happen because containers talk to `io-garage:3900` directly.
evidence: plans/impl/00-contract.md:81 ('`<bucket>.s3.<domain>` routes to Garage's web endpoint 127.0.0.1:3902 for public buckets'), :692 ('Public bucket ... router -> Garage web 127.0.0.1:3902'); plans/impl/02-router.md:39 ('`*.s3.<domain>` (kind `garage-web`, 127.0.0.1:3902)'), :43; src/s3.ts:3 (the daemon's own presigner is path-style, so only the daemon avoids the problem); Garage `[s3_api] root_domain = .s3.<domain>` (06-packaging.md:129) means the API port also accepts these vhosts.
fix: 02 §3 step 1: for hosts matching `*.s3.<domain>` pick the upstream per request: `Authorization: AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 ...` header, or `X-Amz-Signature`/`X-Amz-Algorithm` query, or any method other than GET/HEAD -> Garage S3 API 127.0.0.1:3900; otherwise -> web 127.0.0.1:3902. Record this in contract decision 20 and §10 (the same hostname serves signed API traffic and anonymous public reads). Add `test/router.test.ts` case 'bucket vhost: signed PUT goes to the api upstream, anonymous GET goes to the web upstream' and mention in 05/08 docs facts that both addressing styles work.

section: E. install.sh step 4 (Docker install) and 09-integration-order (integrator VM check); spec §4 'one VPS holds dozens of branches'
problem: Every branch creates its own Docker network (`docker network create`), and dockerd's default `default-address-pools` yield only 31 user-defined networks (172.17-172.31/16 minus docker0 plus 16 x /20 under 192.168.0.0/16). The 32nd branch on the box fails with 'could not find an available, non-overlapping IPv4 address pool', so 'dozens of branches on one VPS' breaks at ~31 regardless of RAM or disk. Nothing in the installer or daemon addresses it.
evidence: src/engine.ts:68 (`docker(['network', 'create', network])` per branch, kept by 05 §4 provisionBranch 'network; ref'); plans/2026-09-08-single-node-serverless-spec.md:171 ('one VPS holds dozens of branches'); plans/impl/06-packaging.md:137 (Docker install step writes no /etc/docker/daemon.json). `docker info -f '{{json .DefaultAddressPools}}'` on a stock install prints null (defaults in effect).
fix: 06 §E step 4: after installing Docker (fresh install only, or when /etc/docker/daemon.json lacks the key) write `{"default-address-pools":[{"base":"10.100.0.0/14","size":24}]}` (1024 /24 branch networks) and `systemctl restart docker` before compose up; skip and warn when a daemon.json already sets the key. Add `--print-daemon-json` to the print renderers and a `test/install.test.ts` assertion. 05 §4 provisionBranch: map the 'non-overlapping IPv4 address pool' error to a 507 with the text 'docker has no free network subnets; see docs/self-hosting/install (default-address-pools)'. Add the fact to 08 install.mdx and to 09's integrator VM checklist (create 40 branches).

section: B. Layout and directory rules (hasPgData / isEmptyOrMissing guards) and H. Copy engine selection
problem: On an unprivileged Linux daemon (local mode as a docker-group user, which is exactly what the e2e `local` job on ubuntu-latest and the XFS CI step run) the postgres entrypoint chowns PGDATA to uid 70 (alpine postgres) mode 0700 on first start. Afterwards the daemon user cannot stat anything inside it: `hasPgData(dir)` and `isEmptyOrMissing(dir)` throw EACCES instead of answering, so every fork start ('every other start requires hasPgData'), the migration skip check and the provision guard fail. §H routes only the fsclone verbs (probe, clone, rm) through the helper container; the two predicates have no helper path.
evidence: plans/impl/04-branching.md:29 ('every other start requires `hasPgData(dir)` (`PG_VERSION` exists)'; 'Guards: `provision` requires `isEmptyOrMissing(dir)`'), :68 (§H: 'run the same verb in the helper container' - verbs are probe/clone/rm only, :9), :108 (CI runs the unprivileged runner against the XFS loop 'exercises the helper engine'); plans/impl/00-contract.md:365-366 (DataDirOps.hasPgData/isEmptyOrMissing have no helper note). `docker run --rm postgres:16-alpine id postgres` -> uid=70(postgres); the image entrypoint chowns PGDATA when started as root.
fix: 04 §B and §H: add `stat` and `isempty` verbs to `src/fsclone.cjs` (print JSON `{exists, pgVersion, empty}`) and make `DataDir.hasPgData`/`isEmptyOrMissing` fall back to the helper container on EACCES|EPERM exactly like clone/rm; contract §4 DataDirOps comment: 'every method falls back to the helper on EACCES'. Add to fsclone.test.ts 'hasPgData on a 0700 directory owned by another uid answers through the helper (mocked docker)'.

section: 8. Background run, R4 health_check (default httpProbe = fetch on the service URL); 06 compose (io-instad env)
problem: The executor's default health probe fetches the public service URL from inside io-instad. In server mode with `INSTA_OSS_TLS=internal` (the e2e server job, air-gapped boxes) Node rejects Caddy's internal CA because the compose stack sets no NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, so every template deploy ends `failed` at health_check with a TLS error; on NAT'd public IPs it also depends on hairpin routing to the box's own public address. The daemon owns the HTTP lane on 127.0.0.1:8080 and can probe it directly.
evidence: plans/impl/05-templates-parity.md:66 ('probe `new URL(healthcheck, url)` same origin else refuse; `httpProbe` (injectable; default `fetch` redirect manual, 5 s)'; 'The health probe goes through the router's HTTP lane'); plans/impl/06-packaging.md:58-71 (instad service env_file only, no CA env); plans/impl/08-docs-e2e.md:69 (server smoke uses `INSTA_OSS_TLS=internal`), :79 (step 9 template deploy over https must succeed).
fix: 05 §8 R4: default `httpProbe` = `http.request({ host: '127.0.0.1', port: cfg.port, path, headers: { Host: new URL(url).host, 'X-Forwarded-Proto': 'https' } })` (loopback into the router's HTTP lane with the service Host; same-origin check stays on the URL); document in 00 §7.1 WP5 that the probe never leaves the box and never needs the CA. Add a templates.test.ts case 'health probe hits 127.0.0.1:<port> with the service Host header, not DNS'.

section: 11. Engine seams: hostAliasesFor; contract §10 row 'Container-to-router path' and 'AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3'
problem: `hostAliasesFor` injects only the branch's minted service FQDNs plus host.docker.internal. Apps also receive `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3=https://s3.<domain>` and agent templates call `https://api.<domain>` (INSTA_API_URL) from inside the container; those names resolve through public DNS. On the e2e server job (`127-0-0-1.sslip.io`) `s3.<domain>` resolves to 127.0.0.1 inside the container (the container itself), and on private-IP or NAT'd boxes it resolves to an address the container cannot reach, so S3 and API calls from apps fail while DATABASE_URL works.
evidence: plans/impl/02-router.md:81 ('`hostAliasesFor(project, branch)`: every FQDN minted on the branch plus its groups' custom domains plus `host.docker.internal`'); plans/impl/00-contract.md:693 (same list), :691 ('AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3 `https://s3.<domain>` (both)'); plans/impl/08-docs-e2e.md:69 (`INSTA_OSS_DOMAIN` default `127-0-0-1.sslip.io`), :75 (`s3_roundtrip` against `https://s3.$DOMAIN`).
fix: 02 §11 and contract §10/§7.1: `hostAliasesFor` = minted FQDNs of the branch + `api.<domain>` + `s3.<domain>` + `<bucket>.s3.<domain>` for every bucket of the branch + custom domains + host.docker.internal, all `:host-gateway` (server mode; local mode unchanged). Extend the server.test.ts region WP2 assertion 'deploy passes hostAliases containing ...' with `api.example.test` and `s3.example.test`.

section: 4. Postgres lane (TLS termination) and 8. Certificates (no default context)
problem: `new tls.TLSSocket(c, { isServer: true, SNICallback })` has no default `secureContext`. A client that sends no SNI (libpq < 14: Ubuntu 20.04 libpq 12, Debian 11 libpq 13, older JDBC and ODBC drivers) never triggers SNICallback, so the handshake aborts with an opaque 'sslv3 alert handshake failure' and the plan's ErrorResponse path ('no database at this hostname (SNI)') is unreachable. The design had a default context; the contract dropped self-signed certs without replacing the default.
evidence: plans/impl/02-router.md:53 ('SSLRequest -> `S`, `new tls.TLSSocket(c, { isServer: true, SNICallback })`, route by SNI'), :69 ('Still missing -> the handshake fails and the lane destroys the socket'), :57 (SNI lanes likewise); plans/impl/00-contract.md:82 (decision 21 removes openssl self-signed); plans/impl/designs/wp2.json:185 (design used `secureContext: certs.selfSigned()`).
fix: 02 §4, §5, §8: set `secureContext: certFor('api.' + cfg.domain)` (Caddy issues it at install time; the installer's `curl https://api.<domain>/healthz` guarantees it exists) as the default for the pg lane and both SNI lanes; when `servername` is empty after the handshake send ErrorResponse 08P01 'no SNI in the TLS handshake: use libpq 14+ or a driver that sends the hostname (sslsni)' and end. Add router.test.ts case 'pg lane server: client without SNI completes TLS and receives the sslsni ErrorResponse'. Document the libpq 14+ requirement in 08 domains.mdx.

section: E. install.sh steps 2-4 (preconditions, Docker) and Docs facts
problem: Apps reach the router at the docker0 gateway (host-gateway) on 443/5432/6379/27017 and the lane range; that traffic traverses the host INPUT chain. With ufw active (default-deny incoming, common on provider Ubuntu images) every in-container DATABASE_URL, S3 and API call is dropped while the same URLs work from outside (published ports bypass ufw). The installer neither detects nor opens this; the WP2 design asked for the rule and the contract left only a docs sentence.
evidence: plans/impl/06-packaging.md:135-138 (preconditions check root, arch, ports; nothing about ufw/firewalld); plans/impl/02-router.md:132 (docs fact: 'a firewall must allow docker bridge traffic to the host's 443, 5432 ...'); plans/impl/designs/wp2.json:197 ('ufw/firewalld on some VPS images drop docker->host INPUT; the installer should add an allow rule'); plans/impl/00-contract.md:66 (decision 5 adopts host-gateway).
fix: 06 §E: add step 3b 'if `ufw status` reports active: `ufw allow in on docker0 to any port 443,5432,6379,27017 proto tcp` and `ufw allow in on docker0 to any port 20000:20999 proto tcp` (idempotent; print the rules); if firewalld is running add the same to the `docker` zone; otherwise print nothing'. Also open 80/443/5432 inbound when ufw is active (the setup URL is unreachable otherwise). Add the rules to `--print-env`-style dry run output and a `test/install.test.ts` grep. Note in 02 docs facts that the installer does this and that a custom firewall must replicate it.

section: §12 Data directory layout (pg/<ref>/<dataId> comment)
problem: The layout says PGDATA is 'uid 999 inside'; `postgres:16-alpine` runs as uid 70. Anything an implementer derives from 999 (pre-chown in the migration, docs on ls output, helper chown) is wrong for the image the plan pins.
evidence: plans/impl/00-contract.md:725 ('pg/<ref>/<dataId>/ PGDATA bind mount (0700, uid 999 inside)'); `docker run --rm postgres:16-alpine id postgres` -> uid=70(postgres) gid=70; plans/impl/04-branching.md:34 pins postgres:16-alpine.
fix: Change the comment to '(0700; owned by the image's postgres user, uid 70 on postgres:16-alpine, uid 999 on the debian variants; the entrypoint chowns on start, the daemon never chowns)'. Mirror in 04 §B.

section: 1.5 sleep.mdx 'what sleep does'; also spec §4 bullet 'Postgres sleeps cleanly'
problem: Docs claim `docker stop` sends SIGTERM and Postgres does a fast shutdown. For Postgres SIGTERM is smart shutdown (waits for clients to disconnect); the clean behaviour the plan relies on comes from the image's `STOPSIGNAL SIGINT`. The sentence is wrong and would mislead anyone who overrides the image or reads it as a rule for other databases.
evidence: plans/impl/08-docs-e2e.md:27 ('what sleep does (docker stop, SIGTERM, 10 s grace, 30 s for databases; ... Postgres fast shutdown'); plans/2026-09-08-single-node-serverless-spec.md:174; `docker image inspect postgres:16-alpine -f '{{.Config.StopSignal}}'` -> SIGINT.
fix: Rewrite as 'docker stop sends the image's stop signal (SIGTERM for apps and managed databases; SIGINT for the official Postgres image, which is its fast shutdown) and waits 10 s (30 s for databases) before SIGKILL'. Add a 04 §C.2 note: never override STOPSIGNAL on the postgres container.

section: Docs facts for WP8 (local mode DNS claim); 08-docs-e2e.md 1.2 install.mdx
problem: The docs fact says macOS does not resolve `*.localhost`. macOS does (mDNSResponder synthesizes any `.localhost` name to loopback), so the `/etc/hosts` instruction for macOS is wrong; the names that do not resolve are inside containers and on Linux without systemd-resolved.
evidence: plans/impl/02-router.md:128 ('DSNs use `127.0.0.1:<port>` because macOS and containers do not resolve `*.localhost`'); plans/impl/08-docs-e2e.md:21 ('`*.localhost` resolution note with the `/etc/hosts` line for macOS and containers'); measured: `dns.lookup('web-demo-main.localhost')` on this Mac -> 127.0.0.1.
fix: Change both to 'DSNs use 127.0.0.1:<port> because containers and Linux hosts without systemd-resolved do not resolve *.localhost; macOS and browsers do' and point the /etc/hosts fallback at Linux hosts without systemd-resolved (the e2e `ensure_host` helper already does this).

section: 4. Postgres lane (direct TLS classification)
problem: The lane reads 8 bytes to classify and, for `0x16` direct TLS (PG17 `sslnegotiation=direct`), wraps the socket in a TLSSocket. Those 8 bytes are the start of the ClientHello and must be pushed back first or the handshake fails; the design had `c.unshift(B)`, the plan dropped it while keeping the 'direct TLS ClientHello routed' test.
evidence: plans/impl/02-router.md:53 ('read 8 bytes ...; classify: `0x16` direct TLS' with no unshift), :98 (test expects direct TLS routed); plans/impl/designs/wp2.json:185 ('Direct TLS -> server mode: `c.unshift(B)` then the same TLSSocket wrap').
fix: In §4 add: 'direct TLS: `c.unshift(head)` before constructing the TLSSocket; plaintext Startup: keep `head` as pending bytes and forward it to the upstream after the probe'.

section: sleep(key, reason) and the compute adapter stop line
problem: Sleep is `docker stop -t 10` on compute containers whose PID 1 is often a shell or an app that ignores SIGTERM (the cloud measured this and interposes a signal-forwarding PID 1). Every idle or eviction sleep of such a service then waits the full 10 s and ends in SIGKILL, so agent templates with state on /data are killed uncleanly on each sleep and eviction under memory pressure is slow. Compute containers are created without `--init`.
evidence: plans/impl/03-scheduler.md:51 ('`runtime.stop(container, kind === 'compute' ? stopGraceSec : stopGraceDbSec)`'); src/adapters/compute.ts:29 (`docker create --restart unless-stopped ...` with no `--init`); insta-compute docs/sleep-and-wake.md §1.4 (PID 1 that does not handle SIGTERM is SIGKILLed; #210 forwarding shell).
fix: 02/03 compute.ts marked line: add `--init` to `docker create` for compute containers so docker's tini forwards SIGTERM to the app (mirrors the cloud's PID 1 forwarding); assert it in test/restart-policy.test.ts and note in 03 docs facts that apps get SIGTERM then 10 s.

section: 0. Listeners per mode (lane port in use aborts startup) and 11. allocLanes
problem: `allocLanes` picks the lowest port free in state, not on the OS, and a lane port already bound by another process aborts daemon startup. On a laptop any process on 20000-20999 (dev servers, other tools) makes the local daemon refuse to start until the operator edits state.
evidence: plans/impl/02-router.md:29 ('A lane port in use aborts startup naming the port'), :81 ('`allocLanes` ... lowest free port in `cfg.lanes.portRange` across all `branch.lanes`').
fix: §11 allocLanes: bind-probe the candidate (`net.createServer().listen(port, bind)` then close) and skip busy ports; §0: at startup a lane port in use logs a warning and reallocates that service's lane (updating `branch.lanes[id]` and invalidating the table) instead of aborting; abort only when the range is exhausted.
